runs.content: Medtronic (MDT) picked up at the previous close ($92.04) — a clean Q1 FY2027 beat-and-raise (EPS $1.45 vs $1.39 est., revenue $9.8B vs $9.55B est., +13.7% YoY, broad-based across Cardiovascular +18.9%/Electrophysiology +29.1%) with a raised full-year guide on both revenue and EPS and only a modest ~3% stock reaction, chosen over today's bigger earnings movers Dell (Burry AI-capex conflict) and GitLab (already up 20%+, disqualified by strategy D's own rule). HPQ hit T1 @ $31.32 (+25.23%), banking ~$417 on the first tranche. ROK was exited discretionarily (−9.66%, −$97) to keep the book at 35 open positions after MDT's entry — no mechanical stop-losses or signal exits on the other 33 continuing positions. Portfolio net P&L: +$2,445 (+4.53% on $54,000).

Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) picked up at the previous close ($160.70) — wide-moat, 5-star-at-flag Morningstar pick with a 22% discount and a Strong Buy analyst consensus (~15% upside to the $185.36 average target), chosen over Clorox (fresh multi-broker downgrades, deteriorating revenue/earnings) and Hershey (already re-rated near its target). Its pending $6B MarketAxess acquisition ties directly into today's dominant headline — a global bond sell-off and the 10-year Treasury yield hitting levels last seen January 2025, compounded by renewed U.S.-Iran Strait of Hormuz tension. F was exited discretionarily (−8.77%, −$88) to keep the book at 35 open positions after ICE's entry — no mechanical stop-losses or signal exits on the other 34 continuing positions. Portfolio net P&L: +$2,504 (+4.72% on $53,000).
